openwrt_wiki.einleitung: Dual band router with 5 fast (100mbps) ethernet ports. Advertised as AC1200 for its 867Mbps (2x2) 5GHz band and 300 Mbps (2x2) 2.4GHz band.  The v1 and v5 have two non-detachable antennas.  The v3 and v4 have four non-detachable antennas.
openwrt_wiki.hinweise_versionen:
The Archer A5 v5 (USA version) is identical to the C50 v5 hardware. It even uses the same TPlink OEM firmware.

<color #ed1c24>The Archer C50 v6 **ES** version is a rebranded C54 which will never be supported.</color> [[https://forum.openwrt.org/t/tp-link-archer-c50-eu-v6-0-5-ghz-interface-not-present/95532/63|Link to forum]]

The Archer C50 v6 CA/EU and RU versions are supported since 24.10.1. Installation instructions are provided in the [[https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/13547/commits/e9ac1b19e0f3d383ab83373c261bfb5527a29521|commit message introducing device support]].

openwrt_wiki.tftp_v1_v3:
<tabbox v1 and v3 instructions>

The only [[https://forum.openwrt.org/t/lede-on-tp-link-archer-c50-but-the-install-instructions-is-in-polish/3446/2|reported method]] for installing through TFTP is not simple. Fortunately the forum users that did it provided a [[https://mega.nz/#!fFAmHBiA!cHmp9pE5z3r9T3C2wuM665QzEx7DiF04Xf1MBbqI_9g|patched image]]. 

If you are okay with using a image made by a third party, make sure that the patched image is named ArcherC50V1_tp_recovery.bin (non-windows users, ensure that the case match, specifically that V1 is capitalized in the filename) and follow the generic TFTP installation procedure.

To build a image yourself, you need to concatenate u-boot (128 KiB) and a Open Wrt image. The steps to do so are explained below in the [[toh:tp-link:archer-c50#v4_instructions|v4 instructions]] section.
openwrt_wiki.tftp_werte_v1:
=== Specific values needed for tftp on v1===

^ Bootloader tftp server IPv4 address  | 192.168.0.66 (on the PC) |
^ Firmware tftp image                  | ArcherC50V1_tp_recovery.bin (that is the file the client looks for) |
^ TFTP transfer window                 | About 7 seconds holding the WPS button |
^ TFTP window start                    | Must power on pressing the WPS button (keep pressing until the WPS light turns on. Then let got of it) |
^ TFTP client required IP address      | 192.168.0.1 (this is the router's ip, it's not important in the tftp process) |
openwrt_wiki.tftp_recovery: ==== TFTP Recovery (De-Bricking) ==== {{page>meta:infobox:dangerous&noheader&nofooter&noeditbtn}} :!: Recovery mode write u-Boot and firmware to adress 0x00000000 on flash. The serial-less TFTP recovery method for the [[toh:tp-link:tl-wdr4300_v1#de-brick_or_oem_installation_using_the_tftp_recovery|TP-Link TL-WDR4300]] also works for the Archer C50. To prepare the recovery file cut the first 0x200 (that is 512) bytes from original stock image. If you fail to follow this step you will brick your device, [[https://forum.openwrt.org/t/lede-on-tp-link-archer-c50-but-the-install-instructions-is-in-polish/3446/2|see]]. dd if=orig.bin of=tplink.bin skip=1 bs=512 The router looks for the address 192.168.0.66 and a file named ''ArcherC50V1_tp_recovery.bin'' (non-windows users, ensure that the case match, specifically that ''V1'' is capitalized in the filename). For the v3/v4 EU version the file name is: ''tp_recovery.bin''. So the dd-command is e.g.: dd if=Archer_C50v3_EU_0.9.1_0.6_up_boot[171227-rel72331].bin of=tp_recovery.bin skip=1 bs=512 You can then follow the normal TFTP recovery procedure. There is a table above, on the “Installation using the TFTP method” section, with all the necessary details. A quick set of instructions is as follows: -Setup your computer to 192.168.0.66 (SubnetMask /24 = 255.255.255.0) and connect it to the router (the port is not relevant). -Start TFTP server and provide recovery file with it. -To activate TFTP Recovery press and hold Reset Button during powering (8 sec.) on until all LEDs stops to blink and the WPS LED turns on.
openwrt_wiki.netzwerk:
==== Network interfaces ====
The default network configuration is:
^ Interface Name   ^ Description          ^ Default configuration   ^
| br-lan           |      LAN & WiFi      |     192.168.1.1/24      |
| vlan1 (eth0.1)   |  LAN ports (1 to 4)  |          None           |
| vlan2 (eth0.2)   |       WAN port       |          DHCP           |
| wlan0            |      WiFi 5 GHz      |        Disabled         |
| wlan1            |     WiFi 2,4 GHz     |        Disabled         |

==== Switch Ports (for VLANs) ====
Numbers 1-4 are Ports 1-4 as labeled on the unit, number 0 is the Internet (WAN) on the unit, 6 is the internal connection to the router itself. Don't be fooled: Port 1 on the unit is number 3 when configuring VLANs. vlan0 = eth0.0, vlan1 = eth0.1 and so on.

^ Port             ^ Switch port   ^
| Internet (WAN)   | 0             |
| LAN 1            | 3             |
| LAN 2            | 4             |
| LAN 3            | 1             |
| LAN 4            | 2             |

==== Opening/closing the case ====

-> [[:docs:guide-user:warranty|Warranty]]

The case of the Archer C50 is composed of 2 pieces:

  * Top cover (bluish)
  * Bottom cover (gray)

  - Remove the two screws on the bottom cover.

=== Putting it back together ===

  - Press until it clicks back nicely to the bottom cover.
  - Put back the screws
openwrt_wiki.seriell:
==== Serial ====
-> [[docs:techref:hardware:port.serial]] general information about the serial port, serial port cable, etc.

Solder a header as shown in the picture or wires with a connector directly. The device uses TTL @ 3.3V and not a standard RS-232 Serial that operates between 3 and 15V, so do not try to connect it to a common serial adapter: you will certainly fry the serial circuit or even the whole board. There are plenty of USB to TTL and RS-232 to TTL available on the market, just be careful with the voltage: the standard is 5V and it may also damage your board. Look for the ones with 3.3V or with both voltages and a way to switch between them.

Don’t forget that the TX pin of the serial port must linked to the RX pin of the router and the RX to TX!
How to connect to the Serial Port of this specific device:\\

{{media:tplink:archerc50:archerc50_serial.jpg?250|Serial Pinouts}}

Resistor R600 and R601 are missing.



^ Serial connection parameters\\ for TP-Link Archer C50 v1 | 115200, 8N1 |
^ Serial connection parameters\\ for TP-Link Archer C50 v3 | 115200, 7N2 |
openwrt_wiki.hardware_mods:
===== Hardware mods =====

The onboard flash chip on these models are SPI flash (e.g. W25Q64BV), it should be possible to replace these with larger capacity chips (e.g. 16 MByte or 32 MByte).  An external programmer will be required to do this, as well as flash layout modifications.

openwrt_git_us_eu.message:
ramips: Archer C50v1: support US and EU versions

For the Archer C50v1, the EU and US versions are differentiated by their
respective HW additional version (0x0 for US, 0x2 for EU).

The stock web interface checks this field before flashing, making it
impossible to flash the current (US) factory image on EU hardware.

However the bootloader does not check this field, making it possible to use
a single sysupgrade image for both hardware.

This patch adds the necessary build bits to generate both EU and US factory
images, and renames the target as "Archer C50v1" since there are as of now
3 different versions of Archer C50 (all with different CPUs).

Signed-off-by: Thibaut VARENE <hacks@slashdirt.org>
